newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-STRUGGLING MIDDLESBROUGH DOCKED THREE POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STRUGGLING MIDDLESBROUGH DOCKED THREE POINTS.

text.p: The English premier league docked struggling Middlesbrough three points on Tuesday for failing to play a scheduled match against Blackburn Rovers in December.
After a five-hour hearing with Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson, the league's disciplinary panel said the club "did not have just cause for unilaterally calling off the match."
They deducted three points leaving the northeastern club languishing four points adrift of Southampton at the bottom of the table and fined them 50,000 pounds ($83,300).
An obviously deeply unhappy Robson left the hearing without commenting, pushing his way through a posse of reporters into a waiting taxi.
The league said the club had the right to appeal and added the issue of compensation for Blackburn would be considered later.
The December 21 match was not played after Robson reported 23 of his professional players were either ill with flu or injured.
The league said the fixture would be re-scheduled.

Middlesbrough have had a wretched run in the league, winning only four of their 22 games this season , despite spending lavishly in recent years on foreign imports such as Emerson and Juninho of Brazil and former Juventus striker Fabrizio Ravanelli.

Earlier on Tuesday in an Italian newspaper interview, Ravanelli, disillusioned with recent events, described the situation at Middlesbrough as truly tragic and criticised Robson's handling of the team.
He said Robson should not have given the players time off at Christmas when the club was performing so badly.
"I can't even get angry any more," the Italian told Gazzetta dello Sport. "What can I do? We are tail enders we have hardly any hopes of salvation and they give us three days off?"
Robson's latest signing is former Inter Milan defender Gianluca Festa who arrived on Tuesday to complete a 2.7 million pounds ($4.5 million) transfer.
